# feat(hfp-025): sign-in

## Task

The API acts as one fixed dev User (`DEV_USER_ID` in `.env`). Every query is already scoped by `owner_id`, so the rest of the app is ready for real users. Decide how researchers sign in, then replace the dev User with the signed-in one.

The decision comes first. Options include email + password, magic links, or passkeys, with sessions held in our own Postgres. Hosted identity providers are probably ruled out by ADR 0001's "no third parties", unless they are EU-hosted and covered by a DPA. Collect only what sign-in needs.

## Parent Story

Hosted-first pivot (ADR 0001). The "then sign-in" in HFP-005's task-list item.

## Blocked by

Nothing for the decision. Sending email (magic links, password reset) may depend on the host choice (HFP-024).

## Acceptance Criteria

### Decision
- [ ] ADR covering the sign-in method, session storage (cookie settings, lifetime, revocation), what personal data is stored, and how an account and all its data are deleted.

### Implementation (may be split into its own issue after the ADR)
- [ ] The API reads the current user from the session; `DEV_USER_ID` is used only in development, or removed.
- [ ] Unauthenticated requests to `/api/projects/*` get 401; the app sends the user to a sign-in screen.
- [ ] Sign-out ends the session on the server.
- [ ] Server tests for signed-in, signed-out and another user's data.

## Suggested label

`ready-for-human` (decision)
